findings.title: Ready returns true before initialization, defeating its documented gate
findings.rationale: Ready is the documented precondition for cache use but returns true unconditionally, so a caller that trusts it proceeds while values is nil and Put panics on the first write. Returning values!= nil enforces the contract the comment states.
findings.remedy: func Ready() bool { return values != nil }

findings.title: Start panics with a nil map write when called before Configure
findings.rationale: Start calls Put with no initialization guard and nothing in the shown code orders Configure first, so an early call assigns into a nil map and the process panics. Check Ready before writing, or initialize values at declaration so the ordering cannot be violated.

findings.title: Cache map has no synchronization or stated thread-safety contract
findings.rationale: Put writes to a shared package map with no mutex, and a concurrent write would be a fatal, unrecoverable runtime error. No concurrent caller appears in the shown code, so this is a contract gap: either document that callers must lock or add a mutex inside Put.

findings.title: save discards marshal and write errors, silently dropping records
findings.rationale: Both the json.Marshal error and the dst.Write error are discarded and save returns nil, so a record that fails to marshal or write is lost while Register reports success. This breaks Register's documented contract that persistence failures are returned, so a caller trusting the doc treats lost records as durable. Marshal failures need unusual inputs (channels, func fields, cycles), but write failures such as a full disk or closed writer occur in normal operation.

finding.title: Write failure and short writes report success
finding.rationale: dst.Write can fail or return a short write; both the byte count and the error are discarded, so a partially written or unwritten record reports success. Register's caller has no way to detect the failure.

decisions.reason: merged into the finding at store.go:9: Same defect as finding 1: an error return inside save is discarded so save reports success. The merged finding names both discarded calls (marshal at line 9, write at line 10), so the write-error site stays actionable.

finding.title: Doc comment promises failure propagation the code never performs
finding.rationale: The comment promises that Register returns any persistence failure, but its only callee save always returns nil, so no failure is ever returned (slop rule 2). A caller trusting this contract will treat failed writes as durable.

decisions.reason: merged into the finding at store.go:9: Contract symptom of the same defect: the doc promise fails only because save swallows the marshal and write errors. Propagating both errors makes the documented contract true, so no separate doc fix remains.

findings.title: Preview and checkout shipping thresholds disagree (6000 vs 5000 cents)
findings.rationale: The two implementations of the shared shipping policy diverge: checkout.go:6 waives shipping at 5000 cents, preview.go:5 at 6000. Smallest remedy: share one threshold constant or one helper between the two functions; the tradeoff is a cross-file reference where there is none today, which is the coupling the duplicated rule was avoiding.

findings.rationale: The suite only exercises now=200 against expires=100, so rewriting the check as now <= expires passes every test while accepting a session at its exact expiry instant, contradicting the strict-before contract in session.go. findings.title: Integer-limit test asserts nothing and cannot fail
findings.rationale: ValidSession is a single int64 comparison that cannot panic, and Go integer overflow wraps rather than panics, so the test passes under any implementation, including one written as expires-now > 0, which returns the wrong result at minint64 now with maxint64 expires. Asserting on the returned bool would pin the behavior the test name promises.

findings.title: Put panics on nil map because nothing calls Configure before Start
findings.rationale: Start (service.go:4) calls Put while values is still nil and nothing in the repository calls Configure first, so every Start invocation panics. Initialize the map at declaration or have Start configure the cache, which removes the hidden ordering contract between the two functions.

findings.title: Ready returns constant true and cannot signal the uninitialized cache
findings.rationale: The accessor contradicts its documented contract by returning true unconditionally, so the one check a caller would use to avoid the nil-map panic in finding 1 always passes. Track a configured flag, or return values!= nil once the map is initialized at declaration.

findings.title: Global cache map is unsynchronized against concurrent access
findings.rationale: Concurrent Put calls, or Put racing Configure, would trigger Go's fatal concurrent-map-writes fault. No concurrent access is demonstrated: Start's single Put is the only shown use and Configure is never called, so this is latent until request handlers touch the cache in parallel. A mutex or sync.Map around values is the fix once that happens.
